minutes.headline: Select Board told the building committee to rescope Ritter/Town Hall, dropping ACE, before returning to voters
minutes.summary: The Select Board spent most of the meeting in a joint session with the Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee, giving direction after the narrow town-meeting/ballot defeat of the Ritter/Town Hall renovation: drop the ACE program from the plan, keep PAC in the building, add an Architectural Preservation District Commission representative, and lower the committee's quorum. The board also heard a legal opinion on the limited authority of the Board of Commissioners of Trust Funds, made several routine committee appointments, declared vehicles and equipment surplus, and received a town manager's report covering the Flat Hill Road bridge repair, sewer delinquency figures, and other items. No new town-meeting date or redesign budget was set.

Adjourn the Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee meeting at 9:16 p.m.

budget_items.topic: Trust fund balances (American Legion Poor, J&M Howard Sidewalk, Worthy Poor, Gazebo Restoration, Lunenburg Post 2838)
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager read the March 25 ending balances of five miscellaneous trust funds under discussion of the trust commission's authority. Documentation establishing terms could be found for only two of the five.
A committee member noted that the town's roughly 2,500 water takers are facing a large future cost range for water infrastructure, cited as a competing capital priority.

budget_items.topic: Hypothetical redesign cost of Ritter/Town Hall plan
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said it would matter a great deal whether a plan change costs a small increase versus a much larger one, and asked whether the architect had been asked for a redesign estimate.

budget_items.topic: ARPA funds shortfall for Building Design Committee
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the Lunenburg Municipal Building Design project's ARPA allocation was reported short at the prior meeting; the architect's outstanding invoice has since been sent, resolving the shortfall.

budget_items.topic: Taylor and Burns architect fees already spent / cost of a redesign
budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed that roughly $185,000 has already been spent with the architect and estimated a redesign might cost in the tens of thousands, contrasting it with the $240 vs $180,000 cost of the prior design iteration.

budget_items.topic: FY26 school budget shortfall and Marshall Park request
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled that schools reported a shortfall and Marshall Park sought funding around the same town meeting, framing why the building project's vote was contested.
The town manager reported total FY25 sewer delinquency and a quarterly breakdown, noting a previously-mentioned 29% delinquency figure was not supported by the data.
The town manager reminded the board that funding was included in the FY26 budget for a grant writer program and that the application package is being finalized for departments.

budget_items.topic: Wallace Park fence/play structure damage estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager reported the damage estimate dropped substantially once actual replacement quotes were obtained, and the claim was forwarded to the insurance company.

budget_items.topic: Estimated values of surplus vehicles and equipment
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager listed estimated resale values for several DPW and police vehicles, some non-operational, being declared surplus.

budget_items.topic: Board of Assessors excise tax abatements
budget_items.what_was_said: A member reporting on the Board of Assessors said there were 17 recent excise tax abatements, versus a historical range and a spike of 427 in 2023.

budget_items.topic: Artisans of Hickory Hills art auction proceeds
budget_items.what_was_said: A member read a letter reporting the resident-organized auction raised over $4,000, funding two scholarships to the high school art program with the remainder going to lake restoration.

decisions.decision: The town manager will work with the treasurer/collector and town counsel to try to locate missing trust-fund documentation before any distribution decisions are made.
The facilities director's committee membership will not be decided tonight; the town manager will discuss it with him first given after-hours meeting demands.
The board agreed to keep the committee's charge modification general rather than naming ACE or PAC space changes specifically.
No formal surplus-threshold policy was adopted, but the board indicated interest in letting the town manager surplus low-value items without a board vote in the future.
The board will not take a formal vote on 56 Car A tonight; a vote will follow within 14 days if and after a court judgment enters, per town counsel's guidance.

what_happened.line: The board told the building committee to rescope Ritter/Town Hall, dropping ACE and keeping PAC, before any return to voters.
The board voted unanimously to add an Architectural Preservation District Commission seat and lower the committee's quorum to four members.
The board deferred a vote on the 56 Car A property, saying a vote will follow within 14 days of a court judgment.
The town manager reported sewer delinquency figures that did not support a rate cited at an earlier meeting.
The board directed staff to search for missing documentation on several trust funds before any distribution decision.

why_it_matters: Dropping ACE from the Ritter/Town Hall plan changes what residents will be asked to fund and vote on at a future town meeting or ballot.
Whether the small trust funds can be distributed for their stated purposes depends on documentation the town has not yet located.
Corrected sewer delinquency figures affect what revenue the town can plan for from that fund.
watch_next: No new town-meeting date or redesign budget for Ritter/Town Hall has been set.
A vote on the 56 Car A property, expected within 14 days of a pending court judgment.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every main vote and on most dollar figures; the differences are mostly caption-misheard names and digits. The one thing to know is that the official minutes record a minutes-approval vote (3-0-1, McLeod abstaining) that ours lacks, and ours records a first Kim Muzzy vote with a 2029 term that the official minutes do not show.
